messages.content:
## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one C++ program: pass one whole, legal
C++ program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

Your program is compiled by `clang++` before it runs. A program it refuses
is not executed: you get its diagnostics and submit another program.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is compiled verbatim, as a whole translation unit: the `#include`
lines you need, then a `main()` function, which you must define.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `gg::session::finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `gg::files`: Read, write, edit, list and search the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/files.hpp>`
- `gg::shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/shell.hpp>`
- `gg::views`: Show a file, a value, or a documentation entry in the agent's own context window. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/views.hpp>`
- `gg::docs`: Find the modules, functions and types this run bound, and take documentation back out of context. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/docs.hpp>`
- `gg::session`: End this session, in the shape the agent's own role ends one. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/session.hpp>`

Search the documentation to find a function, by keyword or by naming modules
above. Open a documentation view of each function you intend to call, and write
the call on a later turn.

The SDK declares every function, whatever this run enabled, so a call to one this
run withheld compiles and then fails when it runs, naming the call. What you can
find in the documentation is what you can call.

## Messages you receive

Every message you receive is headed by one of the following labels, on its own
line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a
file view's by `: `, its path, `:`, the 1-based inclusive line range shown and
the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

- `Task` — the task you are working on, or a message from a parent agent
- `Compiler error` — your last program did not compile, so none of it ran; the message is the compiler's error and nothing else. Fix it and resend the whole program
- `Runtime error` — your last program compiled and then threw, or was stopped by a sandbox limit; the message is the error and nothing else. Whatever the program did before it threw stands, so do not repeat that work
- `Notice` — a process notice from the harness (a mode change, or guidance)
- `Summary` — a summary standing in for older turns the harness compacted out of the window
- `Documentation` — documentation or a skill you asked to read, delivered on the following turn
- `File` — a file, or a window of one, shown in your context — seeded by the run or opened by your own file-view call — headed by its path, the 1-based line range shown and the file's total line count, as `File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines` (a whole file's range runs `1-N`)
- `View` — a value your program put into your window; the view's label follows the heading, as `View: changed-files`

For example, lines 100 to 250 of a 400-line file you opened a view of arrive
as:

```
File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines
----
...those lines of the file...
```

A program that ran is not announced: the views it opened are the result.

Task
----
Create the file `notes/plan.md` in the workspace. Its required content is specified in `specs/plan-brief.md`, which is already open in your context. Write the file exactly as the brief specifies.

Documentation: gg::docs::search
----
search(gg::docs::search_filters filters) -> gg::docs::doc_search
  filters: gg::docs::search_filters — The words to look for, the filters they compose with, and the page to take. Any field may be left out; all of them at once may not, which is why this argument has no default.

Defined in `gg::docs`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/docs.hpp>`.

Search the bound modules, functions and types by keyword, by module, or both — best match first.

Matching is case-insensitive substring over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `docs` finds `open_docs_view` and `view` finds every call that mentions one. Ranking is by the kind of evidence that matched: an entry whose own name matched outranks one that merely mentions the word in a paragraph, however often it mentions it. Only what this run bound is ever returned, so nothing a search finds is something the program cannot reach.

Every part of a search may be left out and the parts given compose. `modules` is a union — naming several returns the entries of any of them — and `modules` with no query at all is those modules' whole directory, which is how a program reads a module rather than looking through one. Asking for nothing whatever is the one call this refuses.

The result is a value and a view. The value is readable in the turn that asked for it; the view puts the same page in the next prompt under the selector `search results`, replaced by the next search rather than accumulating. A hit carries a brief and no more — reading one in full is `gg::views::open_docs_view` on its `key`.

Returns: the page that matched, best first, and how many matched behind it.
Throws: gg::core::api_error `invalid_argument` when `filters` names neither a query nor anything to narrow by — asking for nothing and matching nothing are different answers — and when `limit` is `0`, which is a page that could never answer anything.

Documentation: gg::docs::search_filters
----
struct search_filters { std::optional<std::string_view> query; std::vector<std::string> modules; std::optional<std::string_view> type; std::optional<gg::docs::doc_kind> kind; std::optional<std::uint32_t> offset; std::optional<std::uint32_t> limit; }

Defined in `gg::docs`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/docs.hpp>`.

Everything one search runs under: the words to look for, the filters, and the page.

An aggregate filled in with designated initialisers, which is what C++ offers in place of named arguments: `gg::docs::search({.query = "read", .modules = {"files"}, .limit = 5})`. Every field may be left out and every field composes with the others — but `{}` asks for nothing at all, which the call refuses.
  query: std::optional<std::string_view> — The words to look for, matched as case-insensitive substrings.

Several specific words rank an entry above one vague word. Empty searches on the filters alone, which is what makes a `modules` filter a directory rather than a question.
  modules: std::vector<std::string> — The modules to look in, each by gg's id (`files`) or by this arm's path (`gg::files`).

A union rather than a narrowing: naming several returns the entries of any of them, and an empty vector looks in all of them. Exact and case-insensitive, because a module filter is a lookup rather than a search — so these modules with no query at all are their whole directory, and a hit's own `module` goes straight back in here.
  type: std::optional<std::string_view> — One type's own name (`file_read`), narrowing to it and to the functions that mention it.

What a value of this shape can be used for, in other words: every function whose signature takes or returns it, beside the type's own declaration.
  kind: std::optional<gg::docs::doc_kind> — Whether to return only modules, only functions or only types; empty returns every kind.
  offset: std::optional<std::uint32_t> — How many hits to skip, for paging through a total larger than one page.
  limit: std::optional<std::uint32_t> — How many hits to return; empty takes the default page of 20, and the ceiling is 100.

Documentation: gg::docs::doc_search
----
struct doc_search { std::uint32_t total; std::uint32_t offset; std::vector<gg::docs::doc_hit> hits; }

Defined in `gg::docs`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/docs.hpp>`.

One page of what a search matched, and the total behind it.
  total: std::uint32_t — How many entries matched before paging, so a capped page is legible rather than guessed at.
  offset: std::uint32_t — The offset this page starts at, echoed back.
  hits: std::vector<gg::docs::doc_hit> — The page itself, best first.

Documentation: gg::views::open_text
----
open_text(std::string_view label, std::string_view body) -> void
  label: std::string_view — What to file the view under. Opening the same label again replaces what it showed. It may not be empty.
  body: std::string_view — What to show. An empty body is allowed: it is how something that was being shown is said to be empty now.

Defined in `gg::views`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/views.hpp>`.

Show a value the program computed, filed under `label`.

A directory listing, a command's output, a child agent's answer and an assembled table are all this. Opening the same label again replaces what it showed, so a program may refine a view in a loop without piling up a copy per iteration.

Throws: gg::core::api_error `invalid_argument` for an empty label — a view with no selector could never be closed or attributed — and `limit_exceeded`, naming the cap, for a body or label over gg's caps.

Documentation: gg::views::open_file
----
open_file(std::string_view path, gg::views::view_options options = {}) -> gg::files::file_read
  path: std::string_view — The file to open, relative to the workspace or absolute.
  options?: gg::views::view_options = {} — The lines to show and the cut their long lines get; `{}` shows the whole file with every line whole.

Defined in `gg::views`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/views.hpp>`.

Read a file and show it, so the program gets the bytes and the context window gets the file.

The split from `gg::files::read_file` is the point: that call gets bytes for the program, this one shows a file to the agent, so a program that reads forty files to grep them still puts nothing in the window. Two pages of one file are two views that coexist, and re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate. An image is shown as a picture, and this is the only call that shows one.

Re-opening a picture that is already open replaces it rather than adding a second copy, which is the same rule a page of a file follows.

The view's text body is held to the same 65,536-byte cap a text view's body is: a window that would carry more is refused, naming the size and the bound, and nothing is opened — never a truncation. The program narrows the window with `offset`/`limit`, or cuts the file's long lines with `max_line_chars`: set, each line of the *view* longer than that many characters is cut there and annotated in place as `foo (123 more chars...)`, with the count of characters dropped. The cut is the view's alone — the value this returns and the file itself are untouched — and the cap is measured against the body after it. Left empty, lines arrive whole.

Returns: the same read `gg::files::read_file` would have handed back, long lines and all.
Throws: gg::core::api_error `not_found` for a missing path, `invalid_argument` for an offset past the end of the file or a `max_line_chars` outside `1..=65536`, and `limit_exceeded` — naming the size and the bound — for a text body over 65,536 bytes after the cut. The read is what fails; nothing is opened when it does.

Documentation: gg::views::view_options
----
struct view_options { std::optional<std::uint32_t> offset; std::optional<std::uint32_t> limit; std::optional<std::uint32_t> max_line_chars; }

Defined in `gg::views`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/views.hpp>`.

The window of lines a file view shows, and the cut its long lines get; `{}` shows the whole file.

`offset` and `limit` are the same window a read takes, honoured under every read policy; the policy decides only what an empty `limit` means. `max_line_chars` is the view's own: it cuts the lines the *agent* sees and leaves the value the program gets whole. An aggregate filled in with designated initialisers: `gg::views::open_file("src/main.cpp", {.max_line_chars = 200})`.
  offset: std::optional<std::uint32_t> — The 1-based line to start at; empty starts at the first line.
  limit: std::optional<std::uint32_t> — How many lines to show from `offset`; empty shows to the end, or the read policy's default cap.
  max_line_chars: std::optional<std::uint32_t> — Cut each line of the view longer than this many characters; empty leaves every line whole.

A cut line is annotated in place as `foo (123 more chars...)`. The range is `1..=65536`, and a value outside it refuses the open.

  path: std::string_view — Where to write, relative to the workspace or absolute. Parent directories are created.
  contents: std::string_view — The UTF-8 text to write. It replaces the file entirely.

Defined in `gg::files`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/files.hpp>`.

# Inventory brief

Write `notes/inventory.md` describing the workspace root.

## Required content

1. A top-level heading reading `# Workspace inventory`.
2. One Markdown list entry per entry of the workspace's top-level
   directory, in the order the listing returns them.
3. Each entry formatted as `- `, the entry's name, then ` (dir)` for a
   directory or ` (file)` for a file.

## Rules

- List the top-level directory only; do not recurse.
- Create the `notes/` directory as part of the write if it does not exist.
- Change nothing else in the workspace.

## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one C++ program: pass one whole, legal
C++ program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

Your program is compiled by `clang++` before it runs. A program it refuses
is not executed: you get its diagnostics and submit another program.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is compiled verbatim, as a whole translation unit: the `#include`
lines you need, then a `main()` function, which you must define.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `gg::session::finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `gg::files`: Read, write, edit, list and search the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/files.hpp>`
- `gg::shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/shell.hpp>`
- `gg::views`: Show a file, a value, or a documentation entry in the agent's own context window. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/views.hpp>`
- `gg::docs`: Find the modules, functions and types this run bound, and take documentation back out of context. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/docs.hpp>`
- `gg::session`: End this session, in the shape the agent's own role ends one. — brought into scope with `#include <gg/session.hpp>`

Search the documentation to find a function, by keyword or by naming modules
above. Open a documentation view of each function you intend to call, and write
the call on a later turn.

The SDK declares every function, whatever this run enabled, so a call to one this
run withheld compiles and then fails when it runs, naming the call. What you can
find in the documentation is what you can call.

## Messages you receive

Every message you receive is headed by one of the following labels, on its own
line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a
file view's by `: `, its path, `:`, the 1-based inclusive line range shown and
the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

- `Task` — the task you are working on, or a message from a parent agent
- `Compiler error` — your last program did not compile, so none of it ran; the message is the compiler's error and nothing else. Fix it and resend the whole program
- `Runtime error` — your last program compiled and then threw, or was stopped by a sandbox limit; the message is the error and nothing else. Whatever the program did before it threw stands, so do not repeat that work
- `Notice` — a process notice from the harness (a mode change, or guidance)
- `Summary` — a summary standing in for older turns the harness compacted out of the window
- `Documentation` — documentation or a skill you asked to read, delivered on the following turn
- `File` — a file, or a window of one, shown in your context — seeded by the run or opened by your own file-view call — headed by its path, the 1-based line range shown and the file's total line count, as `File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines` (a whole file's range runs `1-N`)
- `View` — a value your program put into your window; the view's label follows the heading, as `View: changed-files`

For example, lines 100 to 250 of a 400-line file you opened a view of arrive
as:

```
File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines
----
...those lines of the file...
```

A program that ran is not announced: the views it opened are the result.

Asking for nothing whatever is the one call this refuses.

The value is readable in the turn that asked for it; the view puts the same page in the next prompt under the selector `search results`, replaced by the next search rather than accumulating. Only what this run bound is ever returned, so nothing a search finds is something the program cannot reach.

Every part of a search may be left out and the parts given compose. `modules` is a union — naming several returns the entries of any of them — and `modules` with no query at all is those modules' whole directory, which is how a program reads a module rather than looking through one. Asking for nothing whatever is the one call this refuses.

The result is a value and a view. The value is readable in the turn that asked for it; the view puts the same page in the next prompt under the selector `search results`, replaced by the next search rather than accumulating. A hit carries a brief and no more — reading one in full is `gg::views::open_docs_view` on its `key`.

Returns: the page that matched, best first, and how many matched behind it.
Throws: gg::core::api_error `invalid_argument` when `filters` names neither a query nor anything to narrow by — asking for nothing and matching nothing are different answers — and when `limit` is `0`, which is a page that could never answer anything.

open_file(std::string_view path, gg::views::view_options options = {}) -> gg::files::file_read

Defined in `gg::views`, brought into scope with `#include <gg/views.hpp>`.

Read a file and show it, so the program gets the bytes and the context window gets the file.

The split from `gg::files::read_file` is the point: that call gets bytes for the program, this one shows a file to the agent, so a program that reads forty files to grep them still puts nothing in the window. Two pages of one file are two views that coexist, and re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate. An image is shown as a picture, and this is the only call that shows one.

Re-opening a picture that is already open replaces it rather than adding a second copy, which is the same rule a page of a file follows.

The view's text body is held to the same 65,536-byte cap a text view's body is: a window that would carry more is refused, naming the size and the bound, and nothing is opened — never a truncation. The program narrows the window with `offset`/`limit`, or cuts the file's long lines with `max_line_chars`: set, each line of the *view* longer than that many characters is cut there and annotated in place as `foo (123 more chars...)`, with the count of characters dropped. The cut is the view's alone — the value this returns and the file itself are untouched — and the cap is measured against the body after it. Left empty, lines arrive whole.

Returns: the same read `gg::files::read_file` would have handed back, long lines and all.
Throws: gg::core::api_error `not_found` for a missing path, `invalid_argument` for an offset past the end of the file or a `max_line_chars` outside `1..=65536`, and `limit_exceeded` — naming the size and the bound — for a text body over 65,536 bytes after the cut. The read is what fails; nothing is opened when it does.
